definitions.ASI: Artificial superintelligence: a hypothetical AI far more capable than leading humans across most important intellectual activities.
definitions.ECI: Epoch Capabilities Index: a score combining many AI benchmarks. It has no fixed maximum and is NOT a percentage of superintelligence.
definitions.Elo: Arena rating: a comparative score based on human preference comparisons. Differences reflect the benchmark at the stated date, not closeness to AGI or ASI.
definitions.notable: Notable AI model: a research-defined category of significant model releases, not every model ever published.
definitions.performanceGap: Percentage difference between the top American and Chinese Arena ratings in March 2026; not a percentage of progress toward superintelligence.

headline.label: Public evidence of superintelligence
headline.explanation: No independent public assessment establishes ASI under an agreed definition.

headline.explanation: Claude Opus 5.5; October 2026 Epoch Capabilities Index points, NOT percent.

companies.label: Companies
companies.intro: See how selected AI labs' models compare on research tests. Each chart measures a specific benchmark—not progress toward superintelligence.

eci.label: General capabilities (ECI)
eci.description: A composite measure of performance across many AI benchmarks. The scale is arbitrary and has no maximum. These are selected evaluated models—not every company or every recent release.
eci.explain: Higher ECI scores indicate stronger results across the included tests. A 167 score does NOT mean 167% intelligence or 83% progress to ASI.

entries.name: Anthropic
entries.context: Top selected model · independently compiled ECI

arena.label: Model preference ratings (Arena)
arena.description: Comparison of selected top models' Arena ratings by developer, as reported in Stanford's March 2026 snapshot. These rankings can change quickly and should not be described as the newest release order.
arena.explain: Arena ratings reflect comparative human preference judgments. A 1,503 rating is not a 1,503% score, nor a measure of superintelligence.

countries.label: Countries
countries.intro: Compare where frontier-model research and private AI investment are concentrated. A country can lead in one dimension and trail in another.

models.label: Notable AI models released
models.asOf: 2025 releases; Stanford report PDF snapshot Feb. 12, 2026
models.description: Count of notable model releases associated with researchers' institutional country affiliations in calendar 2025. Multi-country models can count under more than one country. These are publication-year counts, not ASI progress.
models.explain: The U.S. has the most recorded notable model releases in this snapshot, but that doesn't prove it is closest to superintelligence. The report's online chapter may show later revised counts.

investment.label: Private investment in AI
investment.description: Private-sector AI investment reported for 2025. Government guidance funds and different reporting standards limit comparability, particularly for China. Money spent is not AI capability.
investment.explain: Investment indicates resources entering the sector, not intelligence attained. Public funding and other spending streams aren't fully reflected here.

methodology.whyNotPercent: There is no agreed, scientifically validated finish line for artificial superintelligence. Turning different rankings into '72% of the way there' would create a false sense of precision.
methodology.howBarsWork: Bars represent the measured value divided by the largest fixed display scale for that one chart. They are just visual lengths—not probabilities, completion rates, or a combination of incompatible metrics.
methodology.sources: Original research is linked below each graph. The tracker is maintained as dated snapshots; it is not a live feed of lab secrets, unpublished results, or a real-time intelligence ranking.
methodology.caution: A higher model benchmark score, more releases, or greater investment does not by itself demonstrate AGI, ASI, autonomy, alignment, or military advantage.
